general_information.Description: The SAP inter-disciplinary capstone project provides IT and BA students with important skills and initial experiences in participating in the SAP projects. With the team size of 3-5 members (*), student can apply knowledges and skills they have learned to the real current projects, including: - Understand the lifecycle of a SAP project - Know what to do in each phase of the project - Understand the terminology used in the project lifecycle - Practice teamwork and how to interact with colleagues in a project implementation process - Ensure the proper implementation of quality requirements and schedule - Do troubleshooting All the documents in the project implementation process and the progress reports are required to write in English. (*): Unless impossible, the team should consist of IT and BA students with a recommended IT to BA student ratio of 3:2. In case of only IT students, the team will have to do all the work assigned to BA students under the guidance of BA lecturer.
general_information.StudentTasks: # Choose appropriate project and form group. # Divide and schedule work among members. # Attend all scheduled meeting with supervisor. # Produce document and product according to project requirement and member work share. # Defend work in front of examination board, showing both project results and individual responsibility. # In case of cheating found, the whole team is not allow to defend. # Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense.
general_information.Tools: Appropriate tools for design and implementation.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify and analyze problems as well as develope and discusse possible solutions.
Configure the enterprise structure and business processes for involved modules in SAP
Implement the solutions, including testing verification in SAP system.
Apply project management principles to SAP project.
Develop professional working style, good teamwork skills, communication skills (including presentation skills) and compliance with the production process
